drug_class: RNA interference (RNAi) therapy / small interfering RNA (siRNA)
purpose: Vutrisiran is used to treat a condition called hereditary transthyretin-mediated amyloidosis, or hATTR amyloidosis, in adults. This is a rare inherited disease where an abnormal protein called transthyretin builds up in your body and damages your nerves and sometimes your heart. This medicine helps reduce that damage and improve your symptoms.
how_it_works: Your liver makes a protein called transthyretin (TTR). In people with hATTR amyloidosis, this protein is faulty and clumps together, harming nerves and organs. Vutrisiran works by blocking the genetic instructions your liver uses to make TTR, greatly reducing the amount of harmful protein produced. Think of it like turning down the volume on a radio signal so less of the damaging protein gets made.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include pain, redness, or discomfort at the injection site, as well as joint pain, muscle pain, and feeling dizzy when you stand up. Some people also experience leg swelling or tiredness. These side effects are usually mild.
warnings: Vutrisiran can lower your vitamin A levels, so your doctor will likely recommend a vitamin A supplement while you are on this medicine. Do not stop taking vitamin A supplements without talking to your doctor first. Tell your doctor if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as the effects during pregnancy are not fully known. Always let all of your healthcare providers know you are taking this medication.
typical_dosing: Vutrisiran is given as an injection under the skin (subcutaneous injection) once every 3 months — that is just 4 times a year. A healthcare provider usually gives you this injection in a clinic setting. The standard dose is 25 mg per injection.
